misconceptions.description: Believing that because the AI names an author or year (for example 'Dale, 1969') the claim is checked
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts a claim because it carries a citation, without opening the source
misconceptions.feedback: A named source is not a checked source. Find the actual work and confirm it says what the AI claims; AI often misattributes.

misconceptions.description: Marking an entire AI reply 'true' or 'false' instead of checking each claim separately
misconceptions.trigger: learner records one verdict for a reply that contains several distinct claims
misconceptions.feedback: Split the reply into one claim per row. A reply can be part true, part fabricated; one verdict hides that.

misconceptions.description: Trusting a precise-sounding statistic (for example '90%') more than a hedged statement, even when no study backs it
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps an exact percentage with no locatable source
misconceptions.feedback: A specific number is not the same as a sourced number. If you cannot find the study, mark it fabricated and drop it.
